turns.t: Morning! It's my hands again. The arthritis. It flared up, since the cold weather started, and I'm back to square one.
I'm sorry to hear that. Which joints, and how bad?
The knuckles and the base of my thumbs, both hands. Stiff and sore, especially in the morning. I can't open jars.
How long does the morning stiffness last?
An hour, an hour and a half. It was ten minutes in the summer.
Any swelling or redness, or fever?
A bit of swelling in the knuckles. No redness. No fever.
Any pain in other joints, like your knees, hips or spine?
No, my knees are okay. Just the hands.
Any rash or dry eyes?
No rash. My eyes are fine.
What are you taking, and how did the treatment go after our last visit?
A gel for the thumbs, I can't remember the name, I got it from the pharmacy. And naproxen, maybe 250 mg, twice a day, on and off.
So the gel you can't name, and naproxen 250 mg twice a day as you recall it. Any other history?
Osteoarthritis diagnosed years ago, and I had a stomach ulcer once.
Do you have any allergies?
Years ago, a rash from penicillin, but I've avoided it ever since.
Thank you. Let me look at your hands. Put them on the table, palms down. ~
Here.
There's bony swelling of the end joints and the base of both thumbs, and tenderness with a bit of warmth in two knuckles, no redness.
Is it getting worse? ~
It's an osteoarthritis flare, as you say, but with the long morning stiffness and warm knuckles, I can't rule out an inflammatory arthritis, such as rheumatoid, on top of it.
Rheumatoid! Oh no. ~
It's a possibility, not a diagnosis. The key difference is the length of the morning stiffness, which is over an hour for you. ~
What do we do? ~
Keep using the gel, warm your hands in the morning, and wear thin gloves in cold weather.
I always forget gloves. ~
Put a pair by the front door. And take the naproxen with food only.
Right. ~
If the knuckle swelling gets worse, you get new swelling in other joints, or the stiffness lasts all morning, come back to see me and I'll arrange blood tests and a referral.
I will. Thanks, doctor. ~
